validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: real, well-documented project, not a GEM-only entity. Independently confirmed by an official Pakistani government notice (mofa.gov.pk, as 'North-South Gas Pipeline' -- the project's earlier name), a wire-service report (Anadolu Agency, 2021-05-28, on Russia's Energy Ministry confirming the intergovernmental agreement), a trade journal (Pipeline Technology Journal, 2021-07-23), a Russian foreign-policy think tank analysis (RIAC, 2021-12-13), and current 2026 Pakistani/Russian press (Times of Islamabad 2026-05; russiaspivottoasia.com bilateral-trade update 2026-07). The sheet's own current_ref (isgs.com.pk official project page + Express Tribune) both returned HTTP 403 to automated fetch this run -- consistent with bot-blocking, not deletion (isgs.com.pk is Pakistan's own implementing state agency and still resolves to a live project page per search snippets; Tribune 403s uniformly across all its URLs in this pass). Per the never-delete-over-403 rule I am NOT flagging those as dead, just adding independently-verified supplements. CLASSIFICATION: Fuel=Gas and PipelineType=transmission are correct -- this is a long-haul onshore transmission trunk moving imported/regasified LNG from Karachi-area terminals north to Punjab demand centers (Kasur/Lahore), not a gathering or feeder line. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 6-pipeline roster: distinct from all of them -- P0452 (Iran-Pakistan Pipeline, Asaluyeh->Sindh) is a different bilateral project bringing Iranian gas in from the west; P0766 (TAPI) is the Turkmenistan-sourced pipeline via Afghanistan; P3173 (Somiani-Nawabshah), P3174 (Off-Shore Gas Pipeline) and P3178 (Sawan-Lahore) are shorter domestic lines with different sponsors, routes, and capacities. No relabel/segment-double-count risk found. ATTRIBUTION: Owner1=Government of Pakistan 74% / Owner2=Government of Russia 26% is the CURRENT, post-2021 restructured split (Russia's original 2015 proposal was for an 85% stake via RT Global Resources, a Rostec subsidiary, which was cut to 26% after US sanctions on RT Global forced a redesign around 2016-2021) -- confirmed independently by RIAC (2021-12) and Times of Islamabad (2026-05), both stating 74/26. Caveat: GEM records the ultimate state owners rather than the named implementing entities (ISGS for Pakistan, and whichever Russian SPV currently stands in for the sanctioned RT Global); that's a defensible simplification given the implementing entity has reportedly been restructured multiple times, but a future pass could add the specific corporate vehicle if one is confirmed stable.

validity.recommendation: Clear StartYear1=2024 (blank it) rather than carry a passed, unmet target date; do not replace with another guessed year until an official FID/construction-start date is announced.
validity.researcher_notes: StartYear1 is recorded as 2024, but the project is still in the pre-construction negotiation stage as of the most current evidence found (July 2026 -- see status_reviews below); no source found reports construction beginning in 2024 or at any point since. This appears to be a stale target-date artifact -- the project has slipped repeatedly (2015 IGA -> 'complete by 2025' claims circulating in 2021 press -> 2021 revised agreement targeting exploratory work 'by end of 2023' -> still under negotiation mid-2026, with one 2026 source citing an expected ~42-month construction period 'once it begins,' with no start date given). Carrying a specific past year as StartYear1 for a Status=proposed row misstates the timeline. I could not find any independently-sourced value to replace it with, so recommend blanking rather than fabricating a new estimate (standing rule 2).

fills.researcher_notes: 1,100 km confirmed by an Anadolu Agency wire report (2021-05-28) and Pipeline Technology Journal (2021-07-23), both independent of GEM and of each other. One outlier found (diplomaticourier.com, 1,040 km) is a minority figure against a consistent majority (aa.com.tr, pipeline-journal.net, offshore-technology.com, RIAC, Times of Islamabad, Business Standard headline) -- treating 1,100 km as the corroborated value.

12.4 bcm/y initial capacity (expandable to 16 bcm/y) confirmed by Anadolu Agency (2021) and Times of Islamabad (2026); consistent with the pipe's 56-inch design flow of 700-800 mmcfd unassisted / up to 2,000 mmcfd with compression reported by Pipeline Technology Journal (12.4 bcm/y = ~1,200 mmcfd, within that envelope).

74%/26% Pakistan/Russia state split confirmed by RIAC (2021-12-13, explaining this is a marked-down revision from Russia's original 85% ask) and Times of Islamabad (2026-05), independent of each other and of GEM.

Karachi->Lahore corridor confirmed. Both sources are more precise than GEM's city-level labels (Port Qasim/Karachi LNG terminals to Kasur, which sits just outside Lahore) -- Lahore/Kasur is a minor precision note, not an error worth changing given GEM's city-level convention.

Diameter was genuinely blank on the sheet. Two sources give 56-inch: Pipeline Technology Journal (2021-07-23, from a Pakistani feasibility study citing 56-inch as the economic optimum for 30-40yr demand) and offshore-technology.com's project database. Tier=medium rather than high: offshore-technology.com's own page is otherwise unreliable on this project (it wrongly claims operations 'commenced in 2025' and oddly cross-links it to the unrelated TAPI project, both database-template artifacts), so I can't be fully confident its diameter figure is independently re-derived rather than copied from the same 2021 feasibility-study announcement that Pipeline Technology Journal reports on. Flagging as best-effort fill per instructions rather than withholding.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Status=proposed is still correct. Most recent independent evidence: a July 2026 Russia-Pakistan bilateral relations tracker (russiaspivottoasia.com) describing the pipeline as one of the 'most ambitious long-term projects' with 'negotiations over its construction continuing between Moscow and Islamabad' -- i.e. still pre-agreement, not under construction. A May 2026 report (Times of Islamabad) similarly describes 'advancing technical and commercial negotiations' on the ~$3B project, with construction (~42 months) not yet begun. No source found reports FID, financial close, groundbreaking, or construction activity at any point 2024-2026; the project remains where it has been since the 2021 revised IGA -- a live, actively-discussed but not-yet-under-construction proposal, not dormant enough (this is under continuous active diplomatic engagement as recently as July 2026) to trigger the staleness/dormancy rule. See the separate StartYear1 spec flag in validity[] -- that date field is stale even though the Status value itself is not.

summary: P3101 (Pakistan Stream Gas Pipeline) is real, correctly classified, not a duplicate of any other roster row, and its 74%/26% Pakistan/Russia ownership, 1,100 km length, and 12.4 bcm/y capacity are all independently corroborated (2+ sources each) -- staged 5 new-ref fills (Length, Capacity, Owner, Location, and a best-effort Diameter=56in fill) plus 1 spec concern (StartYear1=2024 is a stale, unmet target given the project is still pre-construction as of July 2026) and a status_reviews verdict of confirm (proposed) with 2026-07 evidence.
